text:
Recent work supports testing sampled-softmax discrimination before aggressive hardest-negative mining. Wu et al. (2024) show that sampled softmax naturally emphasizes high-scoring negatives; temperature controls this emphasis, with excessively hard negatives potentially dominating gradients. Their ranking analysis concerns DCG, not guaranteed HR@10 improvements. [Paper](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf). “Correcting the LogQ Correction” (RecSys 2025) identifies an important distinction: the positive is always included, whereas negatives are sampled; applying identical proposal corrections to both introduces bias. Its experiments concern two-tower retrieval, so transfer to masked BERT4Rec remains a hypothesis. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331). For explicit ranking objectives, Subbiah et al. (2024) demonstrate sampled WARP/LambdaRank with corrected rank estimates. [Paper](https://research.google/pubs/improved-estimation-of-ranks-for-learning-item-recommenders-with-negative-sampling/).

False-negative handling argues for moderate, adaptive hardness: AHNS (AAAI 2024) adjusts negative difficulty during training to mitigate false-positive and false-negative problems, although its evidence is from collaborative filtering rather than masked sequential modeling. [Paper](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28709). Practical experiment inference: retain one BERT4Rec per category, masked-target training and appended-mask inference; compare uniform sampled softmax against a modest hardness curriculum using the same network’s scores. Exclude known training positives from negative pools, without consulting held-out labels; remaining unobserved items are uncertain negatives. Use proposal corrections only when sampling probabilities are correctly specified—deterministic top-k mining does not justify a simple logQ subtraction. Select using fixed macro validation HR@10. Negative lower-tail margins motivate this comparison but do not establish the cause of weaker recommendations.
